paragraphs.text: The martyrdom of the holy martyrs Justin, Chariton, Charites, Pæon and Liberianus, who suffered at Rome
Chapter 1. Examination of Justin by the prefect

In the time of the lawless partisans of idolatry, wicked decrees were passed against the godly Christians in town and country, to force them to offer libations to vain idols; and accordingly the holy men, having been apprehended, were brought before the prefect of Rome, Rusticus by name. And when they had been brought before his judgment-seat, said to Justin, <quote>Obey the gods at once, and submit to the kings.</quote> Justin said, <quote>To obey the commandments of our Saviour Jesus Christ is worthy neither of blame nor of condemnation.</quote> Rusticus the prefect said, <quote>What kind of doctrines do you profess?</quote> Justin said, <quote>I have endeavoured to learn all doctrines; but I have acquiesced at last in the true doctrines, those namely of the Christians, even though they do not please those who hold false opinions.</quote> Rusticus the prefect said, <quote>Are those the doctrines that please you, you utterly wretched man?</quote> Justin said, <quote>Yes, since I adhere to them with right dogma.</quote> Rusticus the prefect said, <quote>What is the dogma?</quote> Justin said, <quote>That according to which we worship the God of the Christians, whom we reckon to be one from the beginning, the maker and fashioner of the whole creation, visible and invisible; and the Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of God, who had also been preached beforehand by the prophets as about to be present with the race of men, the herald of salvation and teacher of good disciples. And I, being a man, think that what I can say is insignificant in comparison with His boundless divinity, acknowledging a certain prophetic power, since it was prophesied concerning Him of whom now I say that He is the Son of God. For I know that of old the prophets foretold His appearance among men.</quote>

Rusticus the prefect said, <quote>Where do you assemble?</quote> Justin said, <quote>Where each one chooses and can: for do you fancy that we all meet in the very same place? Not so; because the God of the Christians is not circumscribed by place; but being invisible, fills heaven and earth, and everywhere is worshipped and glorified by the faithful.</quote> Rusticus the prefect said, <quote>Tell me where you assemble, or into what place do you collect your followers?</quote> Justin said, <quote>I live above one Martinus, at the Timiotinian Bath; and during the whole time (and I am now living in Rome for the second time) I am unaware of any other meeting than his. And if any one wished to come to me, I communicated to him the doctrines of truth.</quote> Rusticus said, <quote>Are you not, then, a Christian?</quote> Justin said, <quote>Yes, I am a Christian.</quote>
Chapter 3. Examination of Chariton and others

Then said the prefect Rusticus to Chariton, <quote>Tell me further, Chariton, are you also a Christian?</quote> Chariton said, <quote>I am a Christian by the command of God.</quote> Rusticus the prefect asked the woman Charito, <quote>What say you, Charito?</quote> Charito said, <quote>I am a Christian by the grace of God.</quote> Rusticus said to Euelpistus, <quote>And what are you?</quote> Euelpistus, a servant of Cæsar, answered, <quote>I too am a Christian, having been freed by Christ; and by the grace of Christ I partake of the same hope.</quote> Rusticus the prefect said to Hierax, <quote>And you, are you a Christian?</quote> Hierax said, <quote>Yes, I am a Christian, for I revere and worship the same God.</quote> Rusticus the prefect said, <quote>Did Justin make you Christians?</quote> Hierax said, <quote>I was a Christian, and will be a Christian.</quote> And Pæon stood up and said, <quote>I too am a Christian.</quote> Rusticus the prefect said, <quote>Who taught you?</quote> Pæon said, <quote>From our parents we received this good confession.</quote> Euelpistus said, <quote>I willingly heard the words of Justin. But from my parents also I learned to be a Christian.</quote> Rusticus the prefect said, <quote>Where are your parents?</quote> Euelpistus said, <quote>In Cappadocia.</quote> Rusticus says to Hierax, <quote>Where are your parents?</quote> And he answered, and said, <quote>Christ is our true father, and faith in Him is our mother; and my earthly parents died; and I, when I was driven from Iconium in Phrygia, came here.</quote> Rusticus the prefect said to Liberianus, <quote>And what say you? Are you a Christian, and unwilling to worship [the gods]?</quote> Liberianus said, <quote>I too am a Christian, for I worship and reverence the only true God.</quote>
Chapter 4. Rusticus threatens the Christians with death

The prefect says to Justin, <quote>Hearken, you who are called learned, and think that you know true doctrines; if you are scourged and beheaded, do you believe you will ascend into heaven?</quote> Justin said, <quote>I hope that, if I endure these things, I shall have His gifts. For I know that, to all who have thus lived, there abides the divine favour until the completion of the whole world.</quote> Rusticus the prefect said, <quote>Do you suppose, then, that you will ascend into heaven to receive some recompense?</quote> Justin said, <quote>I do not suppose it, but I know and am fully persuaded of it.</quote> Rusticus the prefect said, <quote>Let us, then, now come to the matter in hand, and which presses. Having come together, offer sacrifice with one accord to the gods.</quote> Justin said, <quote>No right-thinking person falls away from piety to impiety.</quote> Rusticus the prefect said, <quote>Unless you obey, you shall be mercilessly punished.</quote> Justin said, <quote>Through prayer we can be saved on account of our Lord Jesus Christ, even when we have been punished, because this shall become to us salvation and confidence at the more fearful and universal judgment-seat of our Lord and Saviour.</quote> Thus also said the other martyrs: <quote>Do what you will, for we are Christians, and do not sacrifice to idols.</quote>

Rusticus the prefect pronounced sentence, saying, <quote>Let those who have refused to sacrifice to the gods and to yield to the command of the emperor be scourged, and led away to suffer the punishment of decapitation, according to the laws.</quote> The holy martyrs having glorified God, and having gone forth to the accustomed place, were beheaded, and perfected their testimony in the confession of the Saviour. And some of the faithful having secretly removed their bodies, laid them in a suitable place, the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ having wrought along with them, to whom be glory for ever and ever. Amen.

latex.p0002: 圣殉道者尤斯定、卡里同、卡里忒、培翁及利伯里安在罗马殉难记
latex.p0003: 第一章　总督审讯尤斯定
latex.p0004: 在非法崇拜偶像者当权之时，颁下恶毒法令，反对城乡中的虔诚基督徒，强迫他们向虚妄的偶像奠酒献祭。于是，这些圣者被逮捕，被带到罗马总督鲁斯提库斯面前。当他们被带到他的审判台前时，他对尤斯定说：\Quote{立即服从众神，顺服君王。}尤斯定说：\Quote{听从我们的救主耶稣基督的诫命，既无可指责，也无可定罪。}总督鲁斯提库斯说：\Quote{你信奉何种教义？}尤斯定说：\Quote{我曾尽力学习一切教义，但最终赞同了真教义，即基督徒的教义，即使它们不为持错误意见者所喜。}总督鲁斯提库斯说：\Quote{那就是令你喜悦的教义吗，你这极其可怜的人？}尤斯定说：\Quote{是的，因为我以正确的\OriginalTerm{信理}{dogma}持守它们。}总督鲁斯提库斯说：\Quote{什么是信理？}尤斯定说：\Quote{就是那使我们敬拜基督徒的天主的信理，我们承认祂是从太初就有的独一者，是整个受造界——可见与不可见——的创造者与塑造者；以及主耶稣基督，天主子，祂曾由先知们预先宣告，将临于人类之中，是救恩的宣告者和好弟子的导师。而我，作为一个人，认为我所能说的，与祂无限的尊威相比微不足道，但我承认有一种先知的能力，因为关于祂——我现在说祂是天主子——曾有预言。因为我知道，古时的先知们已预言祂在人间出现。}
latex.p0005: 第二章　继续审讯尤斯定
latex.p0006: 总督鲁斯提库斯说：\Quote{你们在何处聚会？}尤斯定说：\Quote{各人自择其可能之处；难道你以为我们都在同一地点集会吗？并非如此，因为基督徒的天主不受地方限制；祂虽不可见，却充满天地，且处处为信徒所敬拜和荣耀。}总督鲁斯提库斯说：\Quote{告诉我，你们在何处聚会，或你们将跟随者聚集在何处？}尤斯定说：\Quote{我住在一位名叫马丁努斯的人家楼上，靠近提米奥提尼安浴场；整个期间（这是我第二次住在罗马），我不知道有其他聚会之处，除了他那里。若有人愿意到我这里，我就向他传达真理的教义。}鲁斯提库斯说：\Quote{那么，你不是基督徒吗？}尤斯定说：\Quote{是的，我是基督徒。}
latex.p0007: 第三章　审讯卡里同等人
latex.p0008: 于是总督鲁斯提库斯对卡里同说：\Quote{你再说，卡里同，你也是基督徒吗？}卡里同说：\Quote{我是因天主的命令而成为基督徒的。}总督鲁斯提库斯问妇女卡里忒：\Quote{你说什么，卡里忒？}卡里忒说：\Quote{我是因天主的恩宠而成为基督徒的。}鲁斯提库斯对欧埃尔皮斯图斯说：\Quote{你是什么人？}欧埃尔皮斯图斯，凯撒的仆役，回答说：\Quote{我也是基督徒，已被基督释放；靠基督的恩宠，我共享同一望德。}总督鲁斯提库斯对希拉克斯说：\Quote{你呢，你是基督徒吗？}希拉克斯说：\Quote{是的，我是基督徒，因为我敬畏并敬拜同一天主。}总督鲁斯提库斯说：\Quote{是尤斯定使你们成为基督徒的吗？}希拉克斯说：\Quote{我已是基督徒，并将是基督徒。}培翁站起来说：\Quote{我也是基督徒。}总督鲁斯提库斯说：\Quote{谁教导了你？}培翁说：\Quote{我们从父母接受了这美好的宣认。}欧埃尔皮斯图斯说：\Quote{我乐意听取尤斯定的话。但我也从父母那里学会了作基督徒。}总督鲁斯提库斯说：\Quote{你的父母在哪里？}欧埃尔皮斯图斯说：\Quote{在卡帕多奇亚。}鲁斯提库斯对希拉克斯说：\Quote{你的父母在哪里？}他回答说：\Quote{基督是我们真正的父亲，对祂的信德是我们的母亲；我的生身父母已经去世；我从弗里吉亚的伊科尼翁被驱逐后，来到了这里。}总督鲁斯提库斯对利伯里安说：\Quote{你说什么？你是基督徒，而且不愿敬拜（众神）吗？}利伯里安说：\Quote{我也是基督徒，因为我敬拜和敬畏独一真天主。}
latex.p0009: 第四章　鲁斯提库斯以死亡威胁基督徒
latex.p0010: 总督对尤斯定说：\Quote{听着，你这自诩有学识、自以为懂得真教义的人；你若被鞭打并斩首，你以为你能升入天堂吗？}尤斯定说：\Quote{我盼望，若我忍受了这些，我将获得祂的恩赐。因为我知道，对于所有如此生活的人，天主的眷顾将存留直到整个世界的终结。}总督鲁斯提库斯说：\Quote{那么，你以为你能升入天堂领受某种报酬吗？}尤斯定说：\Quote{我不是以为，而是知道并完全确信。}总督鲁斯提库斯说：\Quote{那么，我们现在就进入当前紧迫的正题吧。你们一起前来，齐心向众神献祭。}尤斯定说：\Quote{没有一个思想正确的人会从虔诚堕入不敬。}总督鲁斯提库斯说：\Quote{若不服从，你们必受无情惩罚。}尤斯定说：\Quote{藉着祈祷，我们可以因主耶稣基督而得救恩，即使我们受了惩罚，因为这对我们而言，将在主和救主更可畏、更公义的审判台前成为救恩和确据。}其他殉道者也如此说：\Quote{你们想做什么就做吧，因为我们是基督徒，不向偶像献祭。}
latex.p0011: 第五章　宣判与执行
latex.p0012: 总督\Person{鲁斯提库斯}宣判说：\Quote{凡拒绝向众神献祭、不服从皇帝命令者，应受鞭打，并依法处斩首之刑。}圣殉道者们光荣了天主，前往惯常的地点，被斩首，并在宣认救主中完成了他们的见证。有些信友秘密取走了他们的遗体，安放在适宜之处，我们的主耶稣基督的恩宠与他们一同工作，愿光荣归于祂，直到永远。阿们。
